D. WHAT TO SAY PLAINLY ABOUT AN AUTOMATED REVIEW
- 'Reviewed' means an automated agent checked each sentence against web-search excerpts and model-generated summaries on a given date. It was not checked against full texts, and not by a clinician or anatomist. Page fetches were refused both on 16 Oct and on 19 Oct.
- The adversarial reviewer is also automated, with the same tool limits. Call it 'a second automated review', never peer review.
- Drawings are original schematics checked against the atlas's notes, not reviewed by an anatomist.
- Name single-source function claims and unconfirmed bibliographic details.
- EMG and longitudinal findings, for example on triceps or hamstring regional growth, may appear only as selectivity claims, never as credit weights.
- Publishing freezes reviewed claims and mapped muscles, so a human or full-text review should happen before each region's version is published, not after.
